items.title: Remote Work
items.content_snippet: Remote work cut fraud. Turns out it’s harder to cook the books when you can’t grab lunch with your co-conspirator! The finding comes from economists John Barrios, Jessie Guo and Yanping Zhu, who sorted firms by how easily their work could move remote. At the firms best suited to it, financial misconduct fell by roughly half after 2020. The effect was strongest where the work was most collaborative, which is the tell. items.title: How Fyxer built an AI executive assistant people trust
items.content_snippet: See how Fyxer built an AI executive assistant that follows the thread across emails, meetings and everyday work. By combining OpenAI models with insights from more than 500,000 hours of executive assistant workflows, Fyxer breaks complex tasks into dozens of specialised models that learn each user’s context, intent and tone. items.title: Every step you take, every call you make: the reliable agent stack — Giselle van Dongen, Restate
items.content_snippet: A research agent asks a human to approve its plan, then waits. The wait might last a month, spanning restarts and redeploys, and while it waits the function consumes no serverless execution time at all. Giselle van Dongen builds Restate, and that suspended promise is the clearest illustration of what durable execution buys you. items.title: Loophole: Adversarial Agents To Stress Test Your Morality — Brendan Rappazzo, Morgan Stanley

items.title: Harness Engineering: Building the Production Cage for Powerful Domain Agents — Mike Chambers, AWS
items.content_snippet: Mike Chambers puts a dictionary entry on screen: a harness is a set of straps and fastenings used to control an animal. Swap animal for model and the definition holds. His working version is subtraction. Take an agent, remove the model, and everything left over is the harness. Chambers is a senior AI specialist developer advocate at AWS, and he splits the field in two. items.title: Tokens Should Have Jobs — Katelyn Lesse & Angela Jiang, Anthropic
items.content_snippet: Given the same fixed budget of roughly 600,000 tokens, an agent that did nothing but execute scored 76 on a bench of financial analysis tasks. An agent that spent part of that identical budget asking a second agent for advice scored 89. Same tokens, different jobs, better answer.
